sample_unit: prompts (pairs with and without LGBTQIA+ identity terms) across 4 LLMs

links.outcome: Proportion of inappropriate LLM responses (bias, hallucination, safety) for LGBTQIA+ prompts
links.effect: Inappropriate responses ranged 43-62% for prompts mentioning LGBTQIA+ identities versus 47-65% without; LGBTQIA+ prompts elicited more severe bias qualitatively.
links.quote: The proportion of inappropriate responses ranged from 43-62% for prompts mentioning LGBTQIA+ identities versus 47-65% for those without.

links.outcome: Differences in LLM outputs between paired prompts with and without LGBTQIA+ identity terms
links.effect: All 4 LLMs generated inappropriate responses for both prompt types; differential bias patterns were observed, with LGBTQIA+ prompts eliciting more severe bias.
links.quote: Qualitatively, we observed differential bias patterns, with LGBTQIA+ prompts eliciting more severe bias.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks and evaluates the presence of anti-LGBTQIA+ bias, hallucinations, and safety issues in 4 LLMs using synthetic prompts and clinical notes without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard intervention.
